title: Common Denominator Worksheets
intro: Teach common denominators with matching wholes.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Partition both strips into pieces of the same size. Record the new numerator as well as the new denominator.

Ask your student

How many new pieces replace each original piece?

If your student needs help

If the student changes only the denominator, count the shaded pieces in the new partition.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each question pairs a proper fraction with denominator 2 through 9 and a unit fraction whose denominator is one greater. For example, a denominator of 5 is paired with a denominator of 6. The least common denominators range from 6 through 90. These consecutive denominators have no shared factor greater than one, so their product is the least common denominator. Do not assume that multiplying the denominators always gives the least one: for 4 and 6, the product is 24 but the least common denominator is 12.
